named_subject: a swan (or duck) floating on water
action: The swan floats with its head lowered to the water for most of the shot, then lifts its neck up into an upright curve over the last four frames.
identity_gap: In frames 1-12 the head-down pose reduces the bird to a closed oval with a small hook at the right, so the doodle's long neck and wedge head only become recognizable in frames 13-16.
notes: Position and timing match the film, where the swan feeds with its head down and then raises its neck near the end; the change from frame 12 to 13 is a sudden pop in head and neck shape rather than a gradual lift. The one change that would help most is adding in-between neck positions across frames 11-13 so the neck visibly rises instead of switching drawings.
